issue: Does the Guidelines' government-benefits loss rule, U.S.S.G. § 2B1.1 cmt. n.3(F)(ii), apply to fraud in government procurement contracts, such as Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) set-aside programs?

sides.position: The government-benefits rule applies to fraud in DBE or similar special procurement programs, because the programs' primary purpose is to benefit small minority-owned businesses.
cases: United States v. Brothers Constr. Co. of Ohio, 219 F.3d 300 (4th Cir. 2000)
United States v. Leahy, 464 F.3d 773 (7th Cir. 2006)
United States v. Maxwell, 579 F.3d 1282 (11th Cir. 2009)

sides.position: The government-benefits rule does not apply to procurement fraud, because procurement contracts are unlike the grants, loans, and entitlement payments named in Note 3(F)(ii); the government expects performance in return for payment.
cases: United States v. Harris, 821 F.3d 589 (5th Cir. 2016)
United States v. Kozerski, 969 F.3d 310 (6th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Stamatios Kousisis, 82 F.4th 230 (3d Cir. 2023)

this_court: The Third Circuit excludes Note 3(F)(ii) for procurement contracts and sides with the Fifth, Sixth, and Ninth Circuits.
quote: There is a circuit split regarding whether the government benefits rule extends to fraud in DBE (or similar special procurement) programs.
cite: United States v. Stamatios Kousisis, 82 F.4th 230 (3rd Cir. 2023)
